story_payload.cover_title: Kavi and the Words to Keep
story_payload.cover_subtitle: A story about listening for what truly helps you grow.
pages: Kavi Monkey was building a leaf kite when two voices flew toward him at once. One friend shouted, 'You will never make it!' Another said, 'Try another way.'
Kavi's mind felt full of noise. The mean words stuck fast, and he almost crumpled his kite before it could fly.
Bodhi Elephant gently tapped his own big ears. 'Listen like Ganesha,' he said. 'A winnowing basket keeps the good grain and lets the dust blow away.'
Kavi listened again. He let 'You will never make it' drift off like dry chaff. He held on to 'Try another way' and 'Keep practicing.'
Kavi changed the kite string, lifted the frame, and the leaf kite caught the wind. This time he smiled, because he knew which words were worth keeping.
Reflection: Which words help you grow, and which ones can you let go like dust?
story_payload.symbol_line: Large Ears -> sift helpful words from noise.
story_payload.mantra: I keep the words that help me grow.
